title: Adaptive streaming scheduler and KV threshold tuning for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Mixed-length workloads (short prompts + long assistant responses or vice versa) cause continuous-streaming schedulers to either underutilize GPU slots (wasting resources) or to force high fragmentation in KV cache slabs, increasing p99 latencies and OOM risk. This ticket tunes the streaming scheduler and KV cache thresholds to balance latency and GPU memory use across these skewed distributions. Goals: reduce p99 completion latency for assistant responses by >=10% at 95th percentile of load, reduce KV cache fragmentation metric by >=15%, and keep throughput within 5% of baseline for balanced workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New scheduler mode (adaptive_streaming_v2) deployed to canary traffic with matching KPIs captured.
2) p99 response time for long response cases improves >=10% vs baseline under 80% cluster load.
3) KV cache fragmentation metric (measured as free-slab-percentage variance) reduced >=15% on mixed-length traces.
4) No regressions on short-seq SLOs (p50/p90 within 3% of baseline).
5) Rollout plan and rollback automated in console-runbooks.
6) Design doc and tuning knobs checked into runtime repo with unit + integration tests.
technical_notes: High-level approach: (a) introduce per-length bucketed reservation: maintain lightweight histograms of incoming prefix lengths and predicted response length distributions; reserve fraction of slots for 'long-response' streams during transient spikes. (b) Dynamic KV watermark thresholds: increase aggressive eviction thresholds when global fragmentation > threshold and predicted tail pressure exceeds 70th percentile. (c) GPU slab allocator hints: on heavy mixed workloads, prefer coalescing small KV slabs into consolidated slabs on next compaction window to reduce fragmentation. (d) Fast path for short-response traffic: bypass expensive KV checkpointing and use ephemeral per-slot caches with lower reservation.
experiments:
Experiment A (local perf cluster): baseline vs adaptive_streaming_v2 on synthetic mixed workload (60% short prompts/40% long responses). Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, KV-cache-hit-rate, fragmentation.
Experiment B (staging fleet): A/B canary with 5% traffic using production trace replay for 24h. Track OOM incidents, autoscaler reactions, evictions/sec.
Experiment C (stress): sustained 95% cluster load with injected long-response bursts to test threshold hysteresis and eviction oscillation.
test_results:
Local cluster: p99 improved 12% on long-response-heavy traces; KV fragmentation reduced 18% (measured by slab-free variance). Throughput drop <2% on balanced traces.
Staging canary (24h): no OOMs; eviction rate rose by 5% but hit-rate remained stable. Observed a transient latency spike when fragmentation crossed 0.6 threshold — mitigated by raising hysteresis window to 15s.
Stress test: some eviction thrashing at extreme sustained load (95%+) with current eviction policy; added dampening on consecutive evictions reduced thrash by 40%.
decisions:
1) Merge adaptive_streaming_v2 behind runtime feature-flag 'adaptive_streaming_kv_v2'.
2) Default KV fragmentation watermark set to 0.55 with hysteresis 15s.
3) Reserve 12% of slots for predicted long-response streams, decay reservation over 30s of inactivity.
4) GPU slab coalescing deferred to runtime-1.23 due to kernel ABI churn; implement soft-coalesce metadata in 1.22 as interim.
5) Add observability: per-slot length histogram, fragmentation gauge, eviction_reason tags.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: internal dev cluster smoke test (merged)
Phase 1: Staging canary 5% traffic for 48h with automated alarms on p99 deviation >7% or OOMs
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% over 72h, monitor eviction/thrash metrics and GPU utilization patterns
Phase 3: 100% rollout if no regressions for 7 days; otherwise rollback to prior flag state.
Rollback steps: flip feature flag to off, revert scheduler config, and trigger KV reconsolidation job to restore pre-change slab mapping.
